name: MemFlow
plain: MemFlow (Dong and Fu, CVPR 2024): optical flow with a motion memory, a RAFT-style network whose update step also reads attention over the frame's motion features. Apache-2.0 code and weights; some training sets are research-only.
summary: MemFlow (Dong & Fu, CVPR 2024): optical flow with a memory of past motion. A RAFT-style network at 1/8 resolution: BasicEncoder feature and context networks, an all-pairs correlation pyramid, a motion encoder and update block of depthwise-separable large-kernel blocks (SKFlow) instead of a GRU, and an attention readout of the motion features of memory frames; convex 8x upsampling. The authors' released weights; the network is ported from DQiaole/MemFlow. A pair (image1, image2) runs as upstream's first frame of a video (empty memory: the readout attends over the pair's own motion features). Paper (video with memory, val_decoder_depth 15): Sintel test EPE 1.05 (clean) / 1.91 (final), KITTI 2015 test Fl-all 4.10 %.

papers.title: MemFlow: Optical Flow Estimation and Prediction with Memory

limitations: Pairs only: the video memory (the keys and values of earlier frames that upstream's inference keeps) is not exposed; each pair runs as the first frame of a video.
The MemFlow-T checkpoints (Twins-SVT encoders) and MemFlow-P (flow prediction) are not ported.

At 384 x 1248, the first MemFlow-KITTI FP16 TensorRT plan gave 4.672 px EPE versus 0.413 px portable on ten pairs. A separate plan with export-only gather sampling matched portable across all 200 KITTI pairs.

The standard checkpoint's standalone 384 x 1248 FP16 TensorRT plan showed a maximum mean absolute flow difference of 2.58 px on an individual KITTI pair and a maximum per-pair EPE change of 3.45 px across 200 pairs.
task_io: Input: two RGB images (consecutive frames). Output: per-pixel motion from the first to the second (dx, dy in pixels).
